Installing and first launch

The download page offers the installer for the computer it is opened on. Each system blocks an app from an unknown developer once, at the first launch.

macOS

macOS 11 or later, on Apple silicon or Intel.

  1. Download Dome-macOS.dmg.
  2. Open Dome-macOS.dmg and drag Dome to Applications.
  3. Open Dome from Applications. macOS refuses the first launch because the app is not notarized by Apple.
  4. Open System Settings › Privacy & Security, scroll to the message about Dome, and select Open Anyway.
  5. Open Dome again and confirm Open Anyway. Later launches open directly.

Windows

Windows 10 or 11.

  1. Download and run Dome-Windows-setup.exe.
  2. When SmartScreen shows “Windows protected your PC”, select More info, then Run anyway. The installer is not signed with a paid certificate.
  3. Open Dome from the Start menu.

Linux

Linux on x86-64.

  1. Download Dome-Linux.AppImage.
  2. Make the file executable: chmod +x Dome-Linux.AppImage
  3. Run it: ./Dome-Linux.AppImage

If Linux reports that no fusermount binary is found, install the fuse3 package.

The window

Dome opens on a new sheet. On the first launch a notice reads “Help › Examples and Help › Take the tour show how Dome works.” It is not shown again. Sheets that were open when Dome closed, saved or not, return at the next launch on the same computer.

The window below shows the Rankine cycle example in the default layout: files and the Workspace at the left, the sheet in the middle, its figure at the right, and the results at the bottom.

Every pane has the same controls at the right of its header: split right, split down, a menu that chooses what the pane shows (for example Math, a figure, the results, Workspace, Files or Reference), and Close pane. The bar between two panes resizes them. On macOS, keyboard shortcuts use ⌘; on Windows and Linux they use Ctrl.

The Help menu

  • Examples: seven complete sheets whose comments explain each step: a first sheet of equations and units, states of water, a Rankine cycle, vapor-compression refrigeration with R-134a, a gas turbine, the Rankine cycle swept over turbine inlet temperature, and moist air cooled with dehumidification. The sweep example opens in the Sweep view and runs.
  • Take the tour: the view tabs, the sheet, the results, the figure, the Workspace, the pane controls, the File menu and the Help menu, one at a time. When the sheet is empty, the tour opens the Rankine example first.
  • Reference: the sheet language, in a pane beside the current panes. The same reference is at the end of Writing a sheet.
  • Manual: this manual, in the web browser.
  • Licences: the components by other authors that Dome is built on, each with its version, copyright and licence.

Updates

A few seconds after launch, Dome asks whether a newer version has been published. When one has, a bar under the header offers it. Nothing is downloaded until Update and restart is selected. Dome verifies the download, installs it and restarts with the same sheets open. File › Check for updates asks again at any time.

The MATLAB toolbox has its own update check; see The MATLAB toolbox.
